newsitem.title: FRANCE: Euro-MPs want stop to open-ended tax exemptions.
newsitem.headline: Euro-MPs want stop to open-ended tax exemptions.

text.p: The European Parliament on Friday demanded an end to open-ended exemptions on duties on petrol and other mineral oils, such as the British and Irish exemption on waste oil reused for fuel.

The European Commission is proposing to update a 1992 directive on minimum excise duty rates on fuels, ending exemptions from duty on fuels used by pleasure boats, air navigation, lighthouses in Britain and Ireland and cars for disabled drivers in Ireland.
Under the Commission proposal -- COM(96)549 -- Britain and Ireland will be able to keep their exemptions on recycled waste oil and differentiated rates of tax on unleaded petrol.
Euro-MPs approved a report by Irish Liberal Pat Cox which said that, as a matter of principle, exemptions should not be allowed to continue indefinitely and should be regularly reviewed.

Exemptions should not be renewed if they disrupted fair competition and the proper functioning of the internal market, or if they contradicted EU policy on environmental protection, parliament's report said.
Zero duties on fuels would also have to be re-examined as part of European Commission proposals for EU-wide rules on the taxation of energy products, Euro-MPs said.

In a debate on the subject on Thursday night, Commissioner Joao de Deus Pinheiro said the Commission could accept parliament's amendments, with the exception of their demands for links to an energy tax, which went beyond the scope of the legislation.
